dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: If you wanna drum up some business, all you gotta do is holler and everyone on the first floor will be able to see you.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Also, you have to come this way to get to the second floor, which pretty much guarantees that everyone attending the expo will notice you guys at some point.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Not bad, huh? Thanks to the spot I saved you, you guys will be drowning in business before you know it!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: ...Your point being?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Cross-referencing Jahoda's current facial expression against database... Confirmed. Analysis suggests that Jahoda hopes we will return the favor.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (You bet I do! At least robo-girl gets it.)

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Okay... How do we do that?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Generating proposal... Complete. Jahoda, the next time you visit the workshop, I will reserve the seat closest to the hallway for you.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: This seat provides priority access to any dessert items delivered from the kitchen. It is also free from window glare and sits at optimal proximity to the teapot.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: By reserving this premium spot for you, I can guarantee you a most enjoyable dessert-sampling experience.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...Is this your idea of a fair trade?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Are you kidding me? That spot's usually reserved for me. I'd never let you take it if I didn't have my dessert budget to consider.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's going on? Jahoda looks upset...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll level with you. Since I saved you such a great spot for your booth and all, could you possibly lend me some technical support, pleeease?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Technical support"?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: This year's expo is way bigger than ever before. Which means there's definitely gonna be more shenanigans going down, too.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Aino, surely you have some kind of contraption that can, like, scare everyone at the expo into compliance, or something? As the manager, I need something I can fall back on in case the you-know-what hits the fan.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hmmm... lemme think...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, if things escalated that far, shouldn't you just report it to Nefer instead of trying to deal with it yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Well, yes, technically speaking... But if, for example, it was somehow kinda my fault to begin with, I'd probably be better off solving it myself on the DL...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay, what happened...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Remember those three kids? Well, that punk who was harassing them wasn't just some random nobody. He was just the one that got picked to stir things up — there's a whole bunch of people here who aren't happy with the booth situation.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Now obviously, they don't have the guts to pick a fight with the Voynich Guild directly. But apparently, they at least have the guts to harass three kids outside the confines of the expo.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: The problem is, I'm not really supposed to get involved with anything that isn't strictly to do with the expo, so the whole thing would kinda be hard to explain to Nef...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Not that I regret what I did. But geez, Jahoda, you sure know how to make life harder for yourself...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, yeah... Sounds like we need to be smart about this.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Aino, do you think you can help Jahoda out?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: ...Fine. Just this once, I guess I can lend you the Clink-Clank Crisis Control Switch.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Agreed. This option meets Jahoda's requirement for an expo-wide intimidation strategy.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: "Clink-Clank Crisis Control Switch"...? What's that?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: This little guy right here. I made it recently after getting myself into a really sticky situation.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: To activate the switch, you just need to give him three taps on the head. If you do that, there's pretty much nothing in Nod-Krai that you won't be able to handle.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Really? So what actually happens when you activate it?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: You'll find out if it comes to it. But I'm only letting you use it once, so you'd better save it for when you really need it.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Okay, cool. I'll take your word for it.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: It's her... the boss of the Spina di Rosula...

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Uh-oh... Things are about to kick off...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What're you worried about, Jahoda?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Shh! Don't you see 'em over there?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Parasol Lady's the head honcho of the Fontainian underworld. Rumor is, she pulled the crumbling organization back together and avenged her father with her own hands. We don't wanna get on her bad side.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: And Eyepatch over there is a merc captain from Liyue. She has a fleet of her own that sails the seas. Most people know to steer clear.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I was worried this expo might not be big enough for the two of them, if you catch my drift... So I kept their booths far apart. Looks like they wound up meeting in the end, though...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: You don't think they're butting heads already, do you? What am I gonna do...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let me handle this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, guys! What's up?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oh! Hey there, partner and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Partner...)

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Can't go far in my line of work without hearing about the President of the Spina di Rosula or the Champion Duelist of the Court of Fontaine. Thought I'd make some friends since the opportunity's presenting itself.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: #Plus, now that {NICKNAME}'s arrived, I wonder if these ladies might just agree to coming aboard for a drink.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: #(What's {NICKNAME} got to do with that...)

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: You're too kind, Miss Beidou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the thing is... Over there is a friend of ours. She's managing the expo, and seeing as you're all big shots where you come from, she was worried you might, um... butt heads.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Is that so? Well, I think you can put her at ease.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Yeah! And if there's anything we can do to help, just say the word.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, there you have it. Nothing to worry about.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: These people are your... friends? How was that even possible?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They don't call me the "Traveler" for nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, it's Lord Sangemah Bay... I wonder what we're in for this time...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: #Well hello! Is that {NICKNAME} and our dearest miss expo-manager, Jahoda? You're in luck — I'm offering a whole host of expo-exclusive discounts. Don't miss out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's not remotely surprised to see Dori here. This event's practically made for her.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Yeah, she attends religiously every year. And she's always the seller who we get the highest number of complaints about...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Complaints? Hmph, every single Mora I make from this expo is a hundred percent legitimate. I've never broken the rules, and my prices are entirely fair. If people regret their purchases and wanna grumble about it behind my back, that's not my problem.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can hazard a guess as to why people might be complaining...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I know, and every dispute ends in your favor after you've peppered the buyer with a million and one reasons why you're not in the wrong. It's just...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Could you maybe not find a way to send every single one of your customers complaining to me this time? I'm begging you, Lord Sangemah Bay... For me, please?

choices.text: So that's why you came to see Dori?

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Hmm... How about this? A special opening sale just for Miss Jahoda — fifty percent off! In other words, I'll do my very best to keep the number of complaints down to no more than half of my customers. Sound good?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Geez, what a bargain...

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Ehh... Works for me, I guess.

choices.text: Just to beg her to rein in the rip-offs?

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: Have you been to the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop's booth yet? They're selling blueprints for a machine.

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: With everything Uncle's taught me, I bet I could build one of those Thwack 'n Smack Defense Bots! We should buy a blueprint!

dialogues.speaker: Ati
dialogues.text: Sounds like a waste of money to me. We should be spending our expo earnings on more important stuff like clothes.

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: But Uncle said the most important thing is that we have fun!

dialogues.speaker: Raya
dialogues.text: Guys, please don't fight...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: *sigh* I hate to break it to you, but I'm afraid no one really comes to this expo looking to buy toys.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: If you make any Mora here, it won't be nearly enough to buy yourselves a blueprint. I doubt it'll even cover your new clothes.

dialogues.speaker: Raya
dialogues.text: #Oh, hi Jahoda. Hi {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I came here to make sure you kids stay safe. So listen carefully: If you want to look around the expo, that's fine — but you need to be extremely careful when talking to any strangers, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: A lot of crazy people show up to this expo — both sellers and buyers. You don't know what they might be capable of. So, if anything happens, don't try to deal with it yourselves — call for me right away. You got that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jahoda's really serious about looking out for these kids...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Well, it's kinda my job. I'm supposed to be the one in charge.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Just take a look around. This booth is the only one being run by a bunch of kids. If there's anyone out there aiming to cause trouble, you can bet they'll start with the weakest target.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Hey look! It's our old pal, Liben!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two! Been a while, hasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That it has.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Wait, you know this guy too? Okay... I'm slowly starting to get why Boss Nef asked you to help me out...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Ah, you must be the expo manager. Was there something you needed from me?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Nope, just checking in. You're just selling a few ordinary items, is that right?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Mhm, that's right.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Okay. I mean, we've got people selling toys this year, so why not...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Hah, you seem confused. In the right environment, ordinary items don't have to fetch an ordinary price, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I'm sure I'll meet someone at this trade expo who recognizes their hidden value.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Cool. Well, you do you. I'm certainly not gonna stop you.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: What about you, friend? Care to do some business?

choices.text: I'll pass...

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: Well, to be honest, I spent most of the ones in my inventory to purchase this batch of goods. The ones you see here are just for decoration.

response.speaker: Liben
response.text: But I'm confident that I can make a killing here, so I'll be sure to make another batch of Boxes o' Marvels should the opportunity arise later.

choices.text: Are you not in the Box o' Marvels business anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, that's a familiar face. Isn't that Wislawa?

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: #Why, if it isn't {NICKNAME}! Knew there'd be some big names here.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Let's get the official business over with first. Unfortunately, you're the first seller at the expo to receive a complaint. We've received word that the muskets you're selling are a few shots away from turning into scrap.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: Well, yeah. It's written here plain as day.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: "Muskets for sale. Condition: extremely poor. The internal grooves have been worn away, and the ammo might be damp. Best practice is to pray that it doesn't explode before each use."

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...Wait, so you weren't speaking in code to cover your tracks?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Code?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Yeah. Sometimes people bring stuff that needs to be kept on the down low, so they dress it up as junk beforehand. Happens on the black market all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: You're overthinking things here — this stuff really is junk. We were just gonna scrap them, but my superiors thought we might as well try and make some Mora off of 'em.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: And who knows? If the prayers are answered and the gun ends up firing a few times... The buyer hasn't totally wasted their money, have they?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Guess not.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: I mean, a weapon on the brink of ruin that's still capable of considerable firepower... Doesn't that just scream "black market" to you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, but who would buy something like this?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Umm... maybe collectors who don't care if it works? And desperados who don't care if it explodes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fair enough...

dialogues.speaker: Lakkaberry
dialogues.text: Welcome to the Treasure Hoarder booth!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Treasure Hoarders have a booth?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Yep, every year. This is the largest legal black market in all of Teyvat. The stuff they dig up is perfect for a place like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But can one person really represent their entire organization?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Hah, no way! "Treasure Hoarder" is just a catch-all title. Their internal structure is crazy complicated.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Thing is, the members who'd apply to set up the exhibits used to give themselves ever more high-falutin' titles. Y'know, to boost buyer confidence.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Over time, it became an unwritten rule that each expo can only have one "Treasure Hoarder booth."

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: The different factions usually duke it out beforehand for the right to take part.

dialogues.speaker: Lakkaberry
dialogues.text: To be honest, I see myself as a member of the Fruity Order first, and a Treasure Hoarder second.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Fruity Order? That sounds familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Lakkaberry
dialogues.text: Of course it does! The Fruity Order is known far and wide for its heroic deeds!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: The Fruity Order's a familiar name around here, at least. They've been winning the Treasure Hoarder expo rights for a few years now. Although, this guy's a new face.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Ugh! This exhibitor's demands are ridiculous...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: This exhibitor is apparently selling some rare Natlanese artifacts, and he's making some extremely unrealistic demands about how he wants them stored.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I know the contract says that we're responsible for storage, but I'm sorry — it's unreasonable to expect us to meet these requirements.

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Unreasonable? These are rare and very fragile historical relics we're talking about! You can't just throw them into a warehouse, okay? They have to be handled with care!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're from the Masters of the Night-Wind, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Tumaini!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, that's Tumaini alright. So what exactly do you need?

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Um... Well, I... I suppose I can use the assigned warehouse if I really have to. Just... don't tell Granny Itztli about this. Please?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nice negotiating with you.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Whatever "Tumaini" means, it seems like it carries even more weight than name-dropping Boss Nef...)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Sir, we don't forbid exhibitors from offering drink samples, but I need to make sure you understand what you're getting into.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Any samples you offer are at your own risk. If anything goes wrong, like if a customer has a bad reaction to one of your products, the expo can't take any responsibility.

dialogues.speaker: Fassbender
dialogues.text: Rest assured, Ma'am, what you see here is 100 percent pure Mondstadt vintage. Straight from the Dawn Winery's cellars, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Wowee. You don't often find Mondstadt wine this far away from home.

dialogues.speaker: Fassbender
dialogues.text: You're telling me... If you try to ship this stuff through the proper channels, all the taxes and tariffs would send the prices skyrocketing.

dialogues.speaker: Fassbender
dialogues.text: But that's where my connections come in! With me, you get Mondstadt wine at Mondstadt prices!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cool! What kind of connections?

dialogues.speaker: Fassbender
dialogues.text: Uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Hey, hey. You can't go around asking people questions like that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whatcha up to, Jahoda?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Just keeping an eye on things... Looking out for any problems that might need me to step in.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Hey, you three. What are you doing here? There should be at least one of you manning the booth at all times.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Accessing booth operation logs... Analyzing... Neb left to try and buy a new blueprint. Ati soon followed to try and stop him. Finally, Raya came to mediate between them.

dialogues.speaker: Ati
dialogues.text: I keep telling you, we don't have that much Mora to spare.

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: I just wanted to have a look, what's wrong with that?

dialogues.speaker: Raya
dialogues.text: Guys, seriously. Stop fighting...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Here's the thing, Neb. Even if you could afford to buy a blueprint, I'm afraid I couldn't allow it.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I know you like building stuff, but these designs aren't for toys like the kind you're used to — they're for weapons which are very complicated to build, and extremely dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: That's a load of baloney, dumpster-diver! My designs are toys too, actually!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Huh? You build a machine that can blast monsters into the sky, and in your mind that's a toy?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: I mean, at the end of the day, is there really that much difference between weapons and toys anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...Not where Knuckle Duckle's concerned, that's for sure...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ugh, that's not the point... Anyway, you there with the brown hair. You want a blueprint?

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: Yeah... I wanna make some Thwack 'n Smack Defense Bots too! I also have some design ideas of my own, and with your bots as the basis, maybe I'll be able to try them out for real...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: I get it. Your head's so full of ideas you wanna bring to life that you can hardly sleep at night. You try eating some snacks to take your mind off things, but it doesn't seem to help anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: Exactly! Exactly! ...But what can I do? I'll never be able to afford one of your blueprints.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hmm... Well, you must have blueprints for the toys you've made too, right? Let's trade. One of your toys for one of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: Really? Thank you so much, Ma'am...? Is it Ma'am, or...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: It's Boss. Boss of the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop!

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: Thank you so much, Boss of the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Huh, that was very thoughtful. Who are you, and what have you done with Aino?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: What's that supposed to mean? I'm a boss, aren't I? A lot of people depend on me. Looking out for them is a big part of the job.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did that really just happen? For a moment there, Aino stopped being a little kid, and acted like a full-on grown-up. ...A grown-up who's shorter than the kids she was looking out for, but still...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Previous records indicate that Aino has a 94% chance of adopting such behaviors when encountering a child in a similar situation to herself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Flins and Illuga! Fancy seeing you here!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. How do you do?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you here to buy some stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: That's our secondary goal. To put it in Mr. Flins' words, it's important for Lightkeepers to spend some time in the land of the living every once in a while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds like something he'd say, yeah...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Mmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you interested in these muskets? Since we're friends, Paimon'll let you in on some insider info. This officer here is basically selling scrap...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Oh, I'm well aware, hehe. The sign makes that quite clear.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...True.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I'm interested in this particular piece because it brings to mind a picture I once saw.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: It featured several Ratniki and a Fatui officer who fought alongside them. The weapon that the latter used was identical to this one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Fatui teamed up with the Lightkeepers?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: That's not unusual. I've heard similar stories from our older members. The owner of this musket must've been a hero who stood against the Wild Hunt as well.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: But why would you sell a hero's firearm?

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: That's just how the rules work on our end. Everyone agreed to it.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: Whether it's a no-name sergeant like me or a renowned hero, our equipment is to be collected and redistributed once we're dust on the wind.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: The stuff that's usable is given to new recruits, and the scrap is sold for whatever price it can still fetch.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: That way, we can at least put it towards feeding the grunts, y'know. Better than following them to the grave.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Huh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A thought-provoking perspective.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: ...I think I'm going to buy this musket, Mr. Flins. Could you tell me a few more stories about it when you get the chance?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Ahem, so what's the situation in need of mediation?

dialogues.speaker: Lakkaberry
dialogues.text: This person's been glaring daggers at me from behind since she arrived... Hey, you! I'm a member of the Fruity Order, you hear?

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: What a coincidence. So am I.

dialogues.speaker: Lakkaberry
dialogues.text: W—Wait, really?

dialogues.speaker: Lakkaberry
dialogues.text: I... first encountered the humor and intelligence of Trendy Zaytun Peach in the "New Tide Anthology." Then, I heard the legend of Intrepid Valberry while I was in the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Lakkaberry
dialogues.text: The more I heard about your order, the more it drew me in. I've been searching for so long, but I was never able to find an actual member...

dialogues.speaker: Lakkaberry
dialogues.text: So when I heard that the Nod-Krai Trade Expo was being held again, I applied under your name... and now, I finally get to meet you!

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: Ugh... It's those idiots stirring up trouble again, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: So what I'm getting is that this guy's an impostor?

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: Our Order's won the expo rights several years in a row, so we announced that we were backing out of the running this year to avoid conflict. Then this guy had to come along...

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: A few of the other groups were looking to duke it out, so imagine their anger when someone claiming to be one of ours snatched the expo rights again...

dialogues.speaker: Lakkaberry
dialogues.text: Well, no one's made any trouble for me... Wait, does that mean you've taken them all out already? Man, I knew it! The Fruity Order's as good as they say!

dialogues.speaker: Lakkaberry
dialogues.text: Can I join?

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: We can't make trouble at the expo. Voynich Guild rules. Once it's all over, meet me at the harbor in Nasha Town.

dialogues.speaker: Lakkaberry
dialogues.text: I see... Alright, I'll be there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, does he not realize what's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: Also, considering our smooth collaborations thus far, a word of advice for the Guild.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: This guy has only been able to keep his head and his booth because the Fruity Order took care of any rival factions.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: But if there's one thing the Treasure Hoarders have in spades, it's sore losers. Since our order has proven untouchable so far, they're sure to find easier targets to vent their frustration on.

dialogues.speaker: "Ruthless Calla Lily"
dialogues.text: So, look after those kids.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Huh. So this guy has been responsible for more than one conflict so far...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Not bad! Tastes just like back in Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Varka? You're here for the expo, too?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: #Oh hey, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. I was only planning to take a look around. Wasn't expecting this pleasant surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Out in this part of the world, even a home-grown Mondstadt apple is a rare treat...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Yes, and on that note, I should advise you that the prices are quite different from what you'll be used to back home.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Not a problem. It's a price worth paying for a taste of home. I'll take the whole batch, and send someone to collect 'em later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The whole batch? ...Looks like you've already made your money back, huh, Liben?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and Varka — since you're looking for a taste of home, have you tried the Mondstadt wine next door? Apparently, he uses special connections to keep the import costs down.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Yeah, I've tried it. It's pretty good, but not "Mondstadt wine" good.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Besides, I wouldn't be able to buy any even if it was. We can't have the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius going around supporting smugglers, can we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that's true... Uh, you're not gonna reprimand him though, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha. Don't worry, I know it's Nefer's rules here. Not out to make life difficult for you.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: If you find yourself at a loose end, come visit our base sometime. I'm gonna get the knights to make some cider outta these apples.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It would be my pleasure.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: You're as generous as they say, Grand Master.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like you've finally made some real profit.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Hey, don't make me sound so incompetent... Though I'll admit, I wasn't expecting to make my money back quite so quickly. Now I can start thinking seriously about my next venture.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where do you plan to make your next fortune?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I'm planning on heading to Snezhnograd, actually. I hear they're running low on lots of supplies because of Project Stuzha. That's a business opportunity if I've ever seen one.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: With any luck, maybe I'll have the pleasure of seeing you there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, good luck out there! Hope you strike it rich!

dialogues.speaker: Fassbender
dialogues.text: I can't believe you came all this way to investigate me... Still, as a member of this expo, I'm protected by the Voynich Guild. There's nothing you can do to stop me.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Heh, I know. That's why I'll be taking this up with them directly.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It's been a while. What brings you here this time? Are you representing the Dawn Winery, or are you here as "Owl"?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Take your pick. Even Owl would take issue with people smuggling the winery's products.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I understand. But please be assured that I would never pit the rules of the Voynich Guild against the interests of the Dawn Winery. Our longstanding collaboration is far too valuable to me for that.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: No faction exists in Nod-Krai that can impose their will on everyone else. The rules we have now are a result of the tug-of-war between them all.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: In any case, I only allowed this gentleman to sell his so-called "Dawn Winery vintage" here because I'm confident that it poses no threat to our collaboration.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...I see. So this isn't from our cellars at all. It's not even from Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Fassbender
dialogues.text: You...

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: I'm guessing you learned a few of our wine-making techniques then brewed your own liquor using local ingredients from Nod-Krai. Imitations like these are no threat to our business.

dialogues.speaker: Fassbender
dialogues.text: I... Just you watch! One day, my wine will leave the Dawn Winery in the dust!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: I'll grant that your wine is a perfectly palatable product. But the fact that you didn't dare to sell it without attaching our name to it speaks volumes.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: That alone tells me that I'll never need to worry about any serious competition from you.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Leaving so soon? Can't I persuade you to come to the Curatorium of Secrets for some tea with me and your two old friends?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there... It sounded like you were discussing some pretty serious business, so Paimon didn't wanna interrupt...

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm afraid I'll have to decline.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That's a shame.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Next time you're back in Mondstadt, pay a visit to the Angel's Share. At least there, I can offer you a genuine Dawn Winery vintage.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Citlali, I've been told that the merchants here are all protected by the organizers. I'm afraid confronting him myself will be more trouble than it's worth.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ugh, do I have to do everything myself?

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Oh, please, Granny Itztli, have mercy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chasca! Citlali! What are you, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It's a long story... Basically, a few members of the Flower-Feather Clan brought word from Nod-Krai that someone was selling "Wayob fragments" at this expo.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Pretty serious stuff. So, I brought Citlali here to get to the bottom of it, and hopefully keep things under control.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Okay, well as it turns out, we've been tasked with mediating any disputes like this.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Are you intending to try and stop me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please, Granny Itztli.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: *sigh* Look, I'm not trying to be difficult, but you don't need me to tell you that our Wayob are not for sale! ...Wait a second...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: This is just a shard of a Wayob pillar... And its power is long gone, so it no longer has any connection whatsoever to the Wayob. So, tell me. How much did they pay you to ship these out of Natlan?

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Umm... about 800 thousand Mora a piece.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Apparently, people outside of Natlan don't know all that much about our culture. Some people take one look at those pillars and start bragging that they've found a Wayob fragment.

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: I didn't wanna correct them, 'cause that way I could drum up the price...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ugh... Forget it. Since you asked me so nicely, I'll let him stay here until the expo's over. No point making a mountain out of a molehill.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, Granny Itztli!

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Oh, thank you, Granny Itztli!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Oh, don't start thinking you're off the hook! Once this is over, you're going straight to Biram to face the music.

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Eek...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, it's Alice and Nicole!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: #Why hello, {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you looking to buy some stuff from Dori?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hehehe, quite the opposite. I am her supplier.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Nicole came up with a delightful new pricing method recently, which I've asked dear Dori to try out. We're here today to see how it's all going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What sort of pricing method is that?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Curious? Well, allow me to explain.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Instead of an amount of Mora, you collect "courage," "kindness," or "happiness" from the buyer.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The key is to make people realize they don't have to be rich. With an excellence of character, even the treasures of the Hexenzirkel are within your reach.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Kinda like... a Seelie guiding intrepid adventurers through various tribulations until they claim their prize. Such fun, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Not for me. We didn't sell much Hexenzirkel gear this time at all. At this point, I'll have to whip out some Sumeru specialties just to break even...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you're actually losing money, Dori?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: You're saying our gifts didn't reach that many people?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I'm saying... we made diddly-squat. Hate to break it to you, Miss Mage, but you don't have much of a head for business.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Oh, it might not have made much, but this has been quite a fun little experiment. To make it up to you, all the revenue from our merchandise is yours to keep, Dori.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Oho! They don't call you a Great Mage for nothing, Miss Alice!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: It's almost time for the expo to end... I'm asking for half a month's leave once we wrap this up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Finally got time to relax, huh, Jahoda?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Yeah, thanks to you. Things are pretty calm right now. Should be smooth sailing from here on out...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Sorry, but I've got a problem over here.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Same here...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (...Jahodaaaaa... You just jinxed it!)

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Someone made off with a batch of my goods using the "goods first, pay later" method. I thought the Guild was the guarantor, but then I went to redeem my money, and... no dice.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: The same thing happened to me.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: "Goods first, pay later?" That convenience is for exhibitors only. It works because their goods stored in the warehouse can be used as collateral.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: The buyer did have Guild-supplied certification.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: In that case, he's one of you. Pick him out of the crowd, and we're good to go.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: ...The person I talked to was a tall, thin young man, but I don't see him here.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: The one who bought from me was on the chubbier side — and nope, no sign of him either.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Wait, so... it wasn't the same person?

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: Miss Jahoda, we need help! Ati went into town a while back, and we haven't heard from him!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: What? Why would he do that?

dialogues.speaker: Raya
dialogues.text: He wanted to use the Mora we got from our exhibit to buy everyone a little something in return for looking out for us, so he headed out alone...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Gods, this kid... Wait, did he have your certification from the Guild with him?

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: Yeah, he's our older brother, so he's in charge of all that stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Oh, this is bad...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, let's not panic. What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Remember those people who targeted Ati a while back? I'm worried they kidnapped him and are using his certification to scam goods off the other exhibitors...

dialogues.speaker: Raya
dialogues.text: Sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This isn't your fault.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Should we rescue Ati first? But Nod-Krai's huge. Where would we even start? We could go for the goods first, but we're dealing with a group. If they split up, it'll be impossible to nab 'em...)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (C'mon, Jahoda, c'mon... You promised Boss Nef you'd uphold the Guild's reputation, and you promised the kids you'd protect them... This is all falling apart!)

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Looks like you're down to your last option, dumpster-diver.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Oh... right! The Clink-Clank Crisis Control Switch!

dialogues.speaker: Robot
dialogues.text: Clink-Clank Crisis Control Switch activated.

dialogues.speaker: Robot
dialogues.text: Awaiting orders... Awaiting orders... Awaiting orders...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Activating the switch gives you temporary control over all the robots in Nod-Krai — if you wanted, you could turn this whole place upside down!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: But it won't last long, so think about what you wanna do first.

dialogues.speaker: Raya
dialogues.text: In that case, let's get the stolen goods back first!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...All units advance to rescue Ati!

dialogues.speaker: Raya
dialogues.text: Miss Jahoda...

dialogues.speaker: Robot
dialogues.text: Orders received... Orders received... Orders received...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With the help of the robots, Ati is quickly rescued, and the people holding him scatter and flee.

dialogues.speaker: Raya
dialogues.text: Ati! You're alright!

dialogues.speaker: Ati
dialogues.text: Sorry... I made you all worry...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If anyone should be apologizing, it's those awful people who took you. You just wanted to repay everyone's kindness.

dialogues.speaker: Ati
dialogues.text: They stole my expo certificate. Did that... cause trouble for anyone?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Let's just focus on one thing at a time...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Inventory complete. All goods have been retrieved.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: See? Told ya. With the Clink-Clank Crisis Control Switch, there's no problem in Nod-Krai you can't handle!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: With so many bots around, we didn't have to choose between the rescue and getting the goods back. We were able to do both!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Aino...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: These kids call me Boss, and as their Boss, it's my job to protect 'em. No way I'm letting them get in trouble with the Guild!

dialogues.speaker: Ati
dialogues.text: Thanks, Boss!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aino's a great person to have on your side, huh.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: To be honest, I could hug you right now... But I think I'll have that vacation first.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Oh, right! I owe you a Hot Dog, don't I?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Jahoda finally catches a break, and is free from further drama for the time being.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: My dear partner, and dearest Paimon, how about testing the latest invention? It's a masterpiece of Fontainian technology, endorsed by the Spina di Rosula and built using theoretical foundations provided by the Fontaine Research Institute!

choices.text: Bring it on! I'm on fire!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah! Let's see what these Pneumousia mechanisms are capable of!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Wonderful! Get ready and remember to have fun!

choices.text: Let's chat!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Navia, you haven't visited Nod-Krai much before, have you? Why don't we show you around?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I've spent a little time here, at least enough to visit every shop in Nasha Town with Clorinde.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It feels like the goods here all have a unique, untamed energy to them — it's something you don't really find on the streets of Fontaine.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ordered and intricate might be pleasing to the eye, but sometimes it can feel like there's something missing — a certain je nais se quois that the chaos of Nod-Krai has in spades...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Like one of those Sumeru vases that open up like a flower when you tap them, emitting light and a fine, cooling mist. Or a pillow with a built-in music box that soothes you to sleep...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks she gets what you're saying. It's like... things become more interesting when they do something unusual, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon completely agrees! Mhm... Compared to something tried and tested — even if it is pretty — it's way more fun to try something new!

choices.text: Speaking of which, where did you buy these?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Really? If you take a left after leaving The Flagship, it's just down the hill. I figured you'd be regular customers!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: The tiny lady who runs the shop is so sweet — she gave me a 20% new-customer discount! I'll definitely take my friends from the Spina di Rosula the next time I visit.

choices.text: I haven't seen anything like them on sale in Nod-Krai...
I've got something else to do right now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. We'll drop by again when we're free!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That's alright, you go do what you've got to do, then head on back, and we'll have some fun!

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}? Is that you? Do you want to try out some cutting-edge warfare? Just remotely control the Guizhong Ballista and rain down a nasty surprise on those monsters from above!

choices.text: I'm ready.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! Paimon's going to give this 110%!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: That's the spirit! Give it your all, and give those monsters a good blasting!

choices.text: About the Alcor 2...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean Beidou's big shiny new ship? Paimon hasn't seen it before!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You must've been building the Alcor 2 for ages — it must be the most powerful ship in the world by now!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Haha, she's definitely one of the most formidable civilian ships out there, but if we're comparing her to the battleships of Liyue, Fontaine, and Snezhnaya, well... I'm not so sure.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Besides, strictly speaking, she's the second ship of the Alcor-class, and the second-biggest in the fleet. We haven't even named her yet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You haven't given her a name? Why not?

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Well, that's quite the story, actually — battleships are usually given a naming ceremony when they're first launched. But the "Alcor 2" sort of skipped the queue a bit.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: We launched her on the same day as another ship — a supply ship — and considering her rather special purpose, we decided to keep things low-key and do away with the naming ceremony altogether.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Then, after she was fully outfitted, she sailed straight out to the open ocean. She was only back in dock long enough for us to verify her new propulsion system was working as planned before we took delivery of another set of new equipment, and she headed back out to sea. It's been quite the journey so far...

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Prior to this latest voyage to Nod-Krai, we hadn't even officially announced her existence. So, we've been calling her "No. 2" all this time, and the name's started to stick!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon feels kinda sad for her, just being called "No. 2"...

choices.text: It sounds like a code name from a spy story...

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Agreed. In fact, we're hoping to name her when she makes her official debut at the trade expo.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: I'll be doing my best to come up with something that fits her stature! Any suggestions would be more than welcome...

choices.text: You should give her a catchy name.
We need some time to get ready for another round.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We're still getting used to this new type of fighting, so we need to work hard to prepare!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: I understand. I look forward to seeing you two in action!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: #Hello, {NICKNAME}! And hello, Paimon! Welcome to the Thwack 'n Smack Defense Bots booth. Would you like to experience the basic tutorial?

choices.text: Tutorial? Sure, that sounds great...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Wonderful. Loading tutorial now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, a special tutorial? How thoughtful!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Aino created this tutorial because she wanted people to not only gain a solid understanding of how the Thwack 'n Smack Defense Bots work, but also to have a good time trying them out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If Aino's putting that much thought and effort into this, she must really be proud of her creations...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Please get ready. The tutorial is about to begin.

choices.text: I still have things to do...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Understood. Feel free to come back and continue with the tutorial at any time. I will be waiting for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See you later then, Ineffa!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, welcome back. Would you like to continue your Thwack 'n Smack Defense Bots experience?

choices.text: I'm really feeling this, let's keep going!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mmhmm! Looks like we've found ourselves a super fun way to practice arranging armies!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: In that case, please get ready. Initiating Simulation Assist Mode — simulated combat will begin shortly.

choices.text: Can we run through that tutorial one more time?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good idea! Paimon's already forgotten how to command those Thwack 'n Smack Defense Bots...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: No problem. Please feel free to ask if there's anything else that requires clarification.

choices.text: Don't you feel tired, Ineffa?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, this is such a big event, and it can't be easy running the Thwack 'n Smack Defense Bots booth. Are you sure you can handle it?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Analyzing visitor traffic data and comparing to previous events...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Analysis complete. Based on variables such as venue size and total footfall, the level of visitor traffic at this booth is comparable to Moon-Prayer Night.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Furthermore, on Moon-Prayer Night, I was also responsible for guiding the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop delegation and ensuring their orderly participation.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: In terms of complexity and level of control, the task of managing the Thwack 'n Smack Defense Bots booth fails to meet the threshold for a "highly difficult" classification.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That means you should be able to complete your assignment easy-peasy, right? Just so long as the visitors to your booth remember to behave themselves.

choices.text: I hope you don't get any unpleasant visitors.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Yes, it is a rather non-demanding task. And if all the visitors are polite, that will make me very happy.

choices.text: But if anyone does forget their manners, we'll be happy to give them a reminder for you!
I'll stop by again later.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've got this, Ineffa! We're going to keep looking around!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Understood. Take care. Initiating Standby Mode...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Although we did encounter a rather unpleasant surprise, our booth should be fine for now... Would you like to continue your duel with the Pneumousia Barrage?

choices.text: Bring it on! I'm on fire!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah! Let's see what these Pneumousia mechanisms are capable of!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Wonderful! Get ready and remember to have fun!

choices.text: Let's chat!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Navia, you haven't visited Nod-Krai much before, have you? Why don't we show you around?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I've spent a little time here, at least enough to visit every shop in Nasha Town with Clorinde.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It feels like the goods here all have a unique, untamed energy to them — it's something you don't really find on the streets of Fontaine.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ordered and intricate might be pleasing to the eye, but sometimes it can feel like there's something missing — a certain je nais se quois that the chaos of Nod-Krai has in spades...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Like one of those Sumeru vases that open up like a flower when you tap them, emitting light and a fine, cooling mist. Or a pillow with a built-in music box that soothes you to sleep...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks she gets what you're saying. It's like... things become more interesting when they do something unusual, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon completely agrees! Mhm... Compared to something tried and tested — even if it is pretty — it's way more fun to try something new!

choices.text: Speaking of which, where did you buy these?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Really? If you take a left after leaving The Flagship, it's just down the hill. I figured you'd be regular customers!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: The tiny lady who runs the shop is so sweet — she gave me a 20% new-customer discount! I'll definitely take my friends from the Spina di Rosula the next time I visit.

choices.text: I haven't seen anything like them on sale in Nod-Krai...
I've got something else to do right now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. We'll drop by again when we're free!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: That's alright, you go do what you've got to do, then head on back, and we'll have some fun!

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, hello there. How wonderful to run into you here in a faraway land...

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: ...Would you like some coffee?

choices.text: Sure, I'll have a cup!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So nice of you to offer, Clorinde!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa... Coffee brewed by the Champion Duelist. If this were Fontaine, Paimon's sure only the creme de la creme would be able to enjoy such an honor!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, if you branded this and sold it at coffee shops, you could make a fortune!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: That's very kind of you to say, Paimon, but it's just a cup of coffee.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: #I was going to brew some for myself anyway, as I was getting a little sleepy minding the booth. Besides, I wanted to offer {NICKNAME} something to thank {M#him}{F#her} for the wonderful cocktails {M#he}{F#she} made me.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: #I had the honor of watching {NICKNAME} masterfully mix up some wonderful drinks, and it inspired me to try my own hand.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: So, after I got back to Fontaine, I headed to my favorite coffee shop and studied the basics of how to be a barista. I guess you could say I have a little experience under my belt now.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Clorinde removes a collection of apparatus from her suitcase, before deftly whipping up three cups of coffee...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Paimon takes a sip, and her eyes open wide like saucers. She gulps the rest of the coffee down. You seem to discern a flavor profile quite unlike any traditional Fontaine coffee you've had before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is delicious — is that a sweetness hiding in the roasted flavor? Paimon usually finds coffee way too bitter, but this is perfect!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Just as you might adopt a different stance when fighting a Tainted Hydro Phantasm instead of an Armored Crab, the same logic holds when making coffee for different people.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: For you, Paimon, I used a less bitter variety of coffee bean and added cocoa and sweetened milk to mellow the taste.

choices.text: Mine has a fruity flavor...

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Spot on! I thought you might find your coffee more energizing with the addition of some sweet and sour flavors. It should give you some extra pep to face whatever trials the expo throws up.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: If I only added tangerine juice, it would have accentuated the tannins in the coffee. That's why I balanced it with apple juice. You look like you're enjoying it?

choices.text: It's wonderful — a fantastic cup of coffee!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Paimon thinks Clorinde is already a pro!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: You flatter me, but real professionals know all sorts of fancy tricks and techniques. I don't see much need for me to put in the hours to learn that high-level stuff.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: I just need to know enough to brew myself a quick pick-me-up at home on the days I don't have time for a leisurely drink at a nice coffee shop.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's such a Clorinde thing to say...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Paimon totally gets where you're coming from. Not everyone's like us, running around learning how to do a million different things.

choices.text: For an amateur, this really is flawless.
Let me guess — you added apple and tangerine juice?
I'll pass this time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks so much, Clorinde! We'll go check out the other booths first and leave you and Navia in peace!

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Alright. But we're not particularly busy, so feel free to come by if you need a rest.
