dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: With Yelan and that lady from the Curatorium of Secrets on the case, everything should be fine. Not to mention, the crew has been fully briefed, and we have contingency plans in place...

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back! Does this mean everything's taken care of and I can rest easy for now?

choices.text: Everything went down without a hitch. How about we continue the drill?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon has a feeling there'll be progress on that end soon! Now, let's get some practice in — who knows when we'll be called on to beat up some more baddies!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Looks like you enjoyed yourself with the Guizhong Ballista... And you're right — we'll get through this like we always do, there's no reason to fret.

choices.text: About the Alcor 2...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean Beidou's big shiny new ship? Paimon hasn't seen it before!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You must've been building the Alcor 2 for ages — it must be the most powerful ship in the world by now!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Haha, she's definitely one of the most formidable civilian ships out there, but if we're comparing her to the battleships of Liyue, Fontaine, and Snezhnaya, well... I'm not so sure.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Besides, strictly speaking, she's the second ship of the Alcor-class, and the second-biggest in the fleet. We haven't even named her yet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You haven't given her a name? Why not?

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Well, that's quite the story, actually — battleships are usually given a naming ceremony when they're first launched. But the "Alcor 2" sort of skipped the queue a bit.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: We launched her on the same day as another ship — a supply ship — and considering her rather special purpose, we decided to keep things low-key and do away with the naming ceremony altogether.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Then, after she was fully outfitted, she sailed straight out to the open ocean. She was only back in dock long enough for us to verify her new propulsion system was working as planned before we took delivery of another set of new equipment, and she headed back out to sea. It's been quite the journey so far...

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Prior to this latest voyage to Nod-Krai, we hadn't even officially announced her existence. So, we've been calling her "No. 2" all this time, and the name's started to stick!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon feels kinda sad for her, just being called "No. 2"...

choices.text: It sounds like a code name from a spy story...

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Agreed. In fact, we're hoping to name her when she makes her official debut at the trade expo.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: I'll be doing my best to come up with something that fits her stature! Any suggestions would be more than welcome...

choices.text: You should give her a catchy name.
We need some time to get ready for another round.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We're still getting used to this new type of fighting, so we need to work hard to prepare!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: I understand. I look forward to seeing you two in action!

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Phew... Thanks to you two, everything's finally settled! This Nod-Krai trip certainly wasn't without its drama, but it's left me feeling thoroughly refreshed nonetheless.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: So, now you've witnessed the mid-air interception capability of the Guizhong Ballista, whaddaya think? Really gets the blood pumping, right? How about another round against enemies on the ground?

choices.text: Let's do it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woohoo! Blasting enemies with the Guizhong Ballista is so much fun, Paimon could happily go another seven or eight rounds — at least!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: That's the spirit! By now, you must feel like you're one with the Guizhong Ballista. Just let rip!

choices.text: About "No. 2"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Paimon seems to remember Beidou saying that the new Alcor ship hasn't been given a name yet?

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Well, I've been toying with a couple of ideas...

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: If the Alcor is meant to be the downfall of every miscreant and monster she meets...

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Then No. 2 should be the vanguard that brandishes a sword to stop them in their tracks.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: I thought the name "Alkaid" might fit. Inspired by a dim variable star I spotted with my astrolabe, it lies at the very end of its constellation — the tip of the sword, if you will.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's certainly very imposing... Paimon can imagine it striking fear into the hearts of all the bad guys who hear it!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Or, we could go another route — this time, we managed to repel the miscreants' attacks with No. 2's on-board weaponry, maintaining justice and order as a result.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: So, another option is "Alioth," meaning "Star of Justice."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's a great name, too! Very... noble! Paimon thinks both names have their charm... Ooh, it's just so hard to choose!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Which name do you prefer?

choices.text: I prefer the name that focuses on striking first and vanquishing your foes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Seize the initiative and strike hard before they know what's hit 'em... that's your style for sure!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Great minds think alike! There's a saying that goes, "prevention is better than cure." Alright, "Alkaid" it is!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: #Alright, then! Let's go with {NICKNAME}'s suggestion and give No. 2 her brand new name!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: Come hang out onboard when you're free. Take the chance to get to know the crew better — you'll love them!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We will!

choices.text: I prefer the name that focuses on standing fast and upholding your principles.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! The reason we fight is to keep everyone safe and happy.

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: You've got a point. Thinking about it, "Alcor" is already intimidating enough. Pairing it with the "Star of Justice" strikes a really great balance.

choices.text: Sounds wonderful. But we've still got a few other places to see first!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now there's nothing left to worry about, you can just take care of whatever comes your way with ease!

response.speaker: Beidou
response.text: I sure can! I look forward to your next visit!

dialogues.speaker: Zhiyao
dialogues.text: Ahoy there and welcome to No. 2, one of The Crux's very finest! It's always a pleasure to play host to the Captain's friends. Make yourself comfortable — mi barco es su barco and all that!

choices.text: Why did you call it "No. 2"?

response.speaker: Zhiyao
response.text: Aha, well, technically speaking, she's the second ship of the Alcor class. There are actually many ships much older than her in the fleet.

response.speaker: Zhiyao
response.text: But, to keep things simple and help with organization, the Captain made a rule — all ships are numbered by their tonnage, biggest to smallest.

response.speaker: Zhiyao
response.text: And by that metric, this beauty is comfortably "No. 2." A lot of our boys have been begging to serve aboard her since she joined the fleet.

response.speaker: Zhiyao
response.text: But of course, with great honor comes great responsibility. No. 2 is slated to patrol the most dangerous waters where she's to keep the shipping lanes free from pirates and monsters.

choices.text: I think I'll take a look around.

response.speaker: Zhiyao
response.text: Of course, but try not to take anything apart — no matter how curious you get. And whatever you do, steer clear of anything dangerous. Do not go around hitting any ammo!

dialogues.speaker: Seahawk
dialogues.text: The nearby waters appear calm for now... No signs of monsters or pirate activity detected.

choices.text: Are you on lookout?

response.speaker: Seahawk
response.text: That's right. I'm the intelligence officer aboard this ship. It's my job to collate information from various sources to help better inform our operational decision-making.

response.speaker: Seahawk
response.text: Before we set sail, I learned a fair bit about Nod-Krai, and it's left me worried about running into pirates. If that did happen, we'd probably have to sink them...

response.speaker: Seahawk
response.text: Or... What if some dirty miscreant crept onto our ship under the cover of darkness to pilfer our supplies? Or even worse, rob us at gunpoint!?

response.speaker: Seahawk
response.text: We're outfitted to be at sea long-term, so we have to manage our resources carefully. The upshot is we don't have a big crew — even minor boarding actions could quickly get out of hand.

response.speaker: Seahawk
response.text: In fact, we ran into a group of pirates a few moons back — nighttime boarding specialists. We took quite the beating before we thankfully managed to drive them off...

response.speaker: Seahawk
response.text: We've identified a whole host of dangerous elements to watch out for in Nod-Krai, but for whatever reason, they all seem scared to mess with this event.

response.speaker: Seahawk
response.text: I can only assume the measures put in place by the organizers are working! I wonder if Captain Beidou has had the chance to talk to the person in charge about teaming up... Long-term partnerships are always a boon to have!

choices.text: (He seems very focused. I should probably leave him to it.)

response.speaker: Seahawk
response.text: The seas are calm and quiet... But that doesn't mean we can let our guard down.

dialogues.speaker: Huoxiang
dialogues.text: #Good day, {NICKNAME}. Officer in charge of surface warfare and land-attack support, at your service!

choices.text: That's quite the job title...

response.speaker: Huoxiang
response.text: It perfectly encapsulates what I do! Captain Beidou has entrusted me with two areas of responsibility. The first is surface warfare, which involves overseeing all of our operations against monsters and pirates on the open sea.

response.speaker: Huoxiang
response.text: The second is to control the improved Guizhong Ballistae to fire specific ammunition according to the signals we send. When intercepting airborne targets, I'll need to select firework trackers in different colors to assess the damage.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And my job is to tell you where to shoot...

response.speaker: Huoxiang
response.text: Yes, once you transmit a signal from the battlefield, I'll fire the ballista from the deck.

response.speaker: Huoxiang
response.text: And the surveillance device you'll be shining on the target is deployed from a separate round launched high above the battlefield. It requires time to prepare — and the window it can remain airborne isn't very long.

response.speaker: Huoxiang
response.text: Of course, right now, this method is limited to single-vessel combat. After all, the Crux isn't intended to face off against entire hordes of monsters in fleet-based operations...

response.speaker: Huoxiang
response.text: Apparently, for particularly demanding missions, the Millelith deploys another kind of surveillance device that's capable of remaining airborne for an entire day, allowing them to keep enemies suppressed with remote fire continuously...

response.speaker: Huoxiang
response.text: Not that I can imagine an enemy that would call for that level of firepower... Neither is it something I'd be eager to see.

choices.text: I'll leave you to it. Keep up the good work!

response.speaker: Huoxiang
response.text: Thank you! I'll do my best!

dialogues.speaker: Gongmiao
dialogues.text: This voyage has been a profitable one, I must say... And the work's been easy to boot!

choices.text: What are you mumbling about? Did I hear something about profit?

response.speaker: Gongmiao
response.text: Ah, the Captain's esteemed guest! There'll be no harm in talking to you...

response.speaker: Gongmiao
response.text: I'm the ship's clerk. My job is to keep track of what we spend and what we earn. Once everything's tallied, I divvy up the profits and give each crew member their share on the Captain's behalf.

response.speaker: Gongmiao
response.text: We took on an escort job for this Nod-Krai voyage — seeing as we were sailing here anyway. It brought in enough to cover our previous expenses.

response.speaker: Gongmiao
response.text: Plus, we loaded hundreds of crates of goods before leaving — there are boxes of high-quality ores and textiles. We'll find someone to sell them for us when we dock in Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Gongmiao
response.text: I wonder how much Captain Beidou will make...

response.speaker: Gongmiao
response.text: A steady stream of income is what the fleet needs to keep growing. If things go smoothly in Nod-Krai, we could find ourselves making more runs there in the future!

choices.text: I wish you every success. Goodbye!

response.speaker: Gongmiao
response.text: Thank you, and the same to you!

dialogues.speaker: Stone Stool
dialogues.text: #Well, I'll be, {NICKNAME}, in the flesh — talk about my lucky day! I head out on deck to get some fresh air, and run straight into you...

choices.text: Aren't you usually on deck anyway?

response.speaker: Stone Stool
response.text: Me? No! I'm the chief engineer. I'm in charge of the ship's propulsion system, which means I'm usually cooped up down below.

choices.text: Does that mean you're always working the oars?

response.speaker: Stone Stool
response.text: Row? Hahahaha! Looks like our techs have done a fantastic job — it's not just outsiders who can't see how the ship works, even folks like you are in the dark!

response.speaker: Stone Stool
response.text: The oars on Alcor-class ships serve a supplementary role. The main propulsion comes from mechanically powered paddle wheels on the surface and propellers beneath the water's surface.

response.speaker: Stone Stool
response.text: If we ever run into a fast-moving monster like a Vishap, we'll need enough speed to either keep up with it or make a clean getaway. In a situation like that, it takes the paddle wheels and propellers to give us the power we need.

response.speaker: Stone Stool
response.text: The oars on either side, which can be hooked up directly to the ship's propulsion device, are usually put to use in rough seas to provide torque, keep the hull steady, and make quick, sharp turns.

response.speaker: Stone Stool
response.text: For example, a good while back, we ran into Beisht — even though the waves were pounding, we managed to keep the Alcor upright by running the oars in an alternating pattern.

response.speaker: Stone Stool
response.text: Plus, when monsters get close and creep up on our blind spots, we can run the oars like weapons to keep them from reaching the waterline and climbing up onto the deck.

choices.text: Like a flail!

response.speaker: Stone Stool
response.text: But of course, we still get good use out of our sails. When the winds howl above the raging seas, harnessing their power can really help us save resources.

choices.text: That never occurred to me before...
That must be very physically demanding...
Enjoy your fresh air!

response.speaker: Stone Stool
response.text: Thanks! You take care of yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Fengyun
dialogues.text: Alright, we still have enough canned, dried, and frozen provisions. But seeing as we're near the coast, we might as well try to get some more fresh food...

choices.text: Are you the ship's cook?

response.speaker: Fengyun
response.text: Me? No, no, no. I look after the ship's stores and supplies. The cook's busy below deck.

response.speaker: Fengyun
response.text: It's just too bad that all we have to hand is canned food and dried or frozen supplies. Otherwise, I'd have him whip you up a feast!

choices.text: That sounds rough.

response.speaker: Fengyun
response.text: Well, it's not that bad...

response.speaker: Fengyun
response.text: I heard that back in the day, sailors had to stick to a strict routine for their meals — once you left port, you'd eat the perishables first, then ration the rest day by day...

response.speaker: Fengyun
response.text: ...Until all you had left were biscuits and bread so stale, it might as well be bricks. Now, that's rough...

response.speaker: Fengyun
response.text: The preservation techniques we have these days are so much better! Our meals might not count as fine dining, but at least everything's reasonably fresh and nutritious.

response.speaker: Fengyun
response.text: Switching out Cryo potions and Mist Flowers is a breeze compared to cutting the rotten bits off perishable food, at any rate.

response.speaker: Fengyun
response.text: You know, back then, I didn't understand why the Captain was always sending people ashore to ask about the latest tech or spending huge sums of Mora to have the latest contraptions hauled aboard...

response.speaker: Fengyun
response.text: But now, I totally get it. I'll never doubt her judgment again!

choices.text: How do you have the strength to sail the seas without proper meals?
I'll leave you to it, then. Bye.

response.speaker: Fengyun
response.text: Alright... Hit me up beforehand the next time you drop by for a meal!

dialogues.speaker: Fassbender
dialogues.text: These Nod-Krai ingredients are fascinating. Their properties are nothing like anything from Mondstadt. I really must find a way to...

dialogues.speaker: Fassbender
dialogues.text: Oh, a customer, is it? Welcome... Please feel free to browse. I've just got a few things I need to take care of here.

dialogues.speaker: Fassbender
dialogues.text: But please be aware, I can't sell you any alcohol if you're underage! Not even here in Nod-Krai!

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: Is this a tragedy or a stroke of luck?

dialogues.speaker: Nkrumah
dialogues.text: *sigh* Guess I have no choice but to keep looking over my shoulder.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: Please do remember to take appropriate precautions and put on protective gear before using these in the field...

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: #Oh? {NICKNAME}, I didn't know you were interested in vintage muskets?

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: You're free to browse, but someone of your abilities really does deserve a newer, high-end, custom model... along with a dedicated gunsmith to keep it in tip-top condition.

dialogues.speaker: Lakkaberry
dialogues.text: If... If I do manage to join the Order, I wonder what nickname they'll give me?

dialogues.speaker: Lakkaberry
dialogues.text: "Savage"? "Fierce"? "Barbaric"? They all sound cool to me!

dialogues.speaker: Ati
dialogues.text: I really should take a walk around if I get the chance and look for some deals on household goods...

dialogues.speaker: Ati
dialogues.text: Clothing, crockery, bedding... Maybe there's a steal waiting for me somewhere?

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: I wish I could make an awesome mechanism...

dialogues.speaker: Neb
dialogues.text: I've already learned so much from my uncle... But it's true what they say — you can't do a thing without mora.

dialogues.speaker: Raya
dialogues.text: Look at the crowd here! And so many new and interesting things...

dialogues.speaker: Raya
dialogues.text: If only everyone could get along with each other and there wasn't so much arguing...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: #Oh, hello, {NICKNAME}! Welcome!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I just so happen to have amassed a collection of valuable, interesting, and highly useful items for your perusal...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: #And just for you, an exclusive {NICKNAME} discount, 50% off everything!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Doing business this far to the north requires traveling a long way...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: That means acquiring a large quantity of goods in advance and transporting everything all in one go by Sumpter Beast or caravan... But what's likely to sell well?
